title: Better Telecom Stock: AT&T vs. Verizon Communications
author: Robert Izquierdo
description: AT&T and Verizon are compared as investment options for 2026. AT&T has improved profitability with a 17.4% net margin after divesting media assets, while Verizon has pursued aggressive acquisitions to expand fiber and broadband capabilities. Despite AT&T's higher net margin and lower valuation, the analyst recommends Verizon due to its superior dividend track record (20 consecutive years of increases, 6.57% yield vs. AT&T's 4.94%), stronger free cash flow, and more attractive forward P/E ratio, despite higher debt levels from recent acquisitions.

Competitive pressures and regulatory risks also present concerns.

title: Telecom Stocks Tumble After SpaceX Spectrum Deal: ETFs in Focus
author: Na
description: SpaceX agreed to acquire a nationwide spectrum portfolio from Grain Management to expand Starlink's satellite internet into mobile services, causing major telecom stocks to plunge on October 10. Verizon dropped 8.75%, T-Mobile fell 13.27%, and AT&T declined 9.81%, marking their worst days in years. However, analysts believe established carriers face limited near-term competition as building a rival network would require substantial time and investment. Space-focused ETFs are expected to benefit long-term from the deal.

title: Here's the 1 Thing I'd Wait to See Before Buying SpaceX Stock.
author: Leo Sun
description: SpaceX stock has declined from its IPO high despite strong growth prospects in Starlink and Starship. However, the company's AI business segment is a major concern, with operating losses widening from $2.46 billion to $3.73 billion in H1 2026, erasing Starlink's $2.84 billion operating profit. At a 49x sales valuation with a $2.2 trillion market cap, the analyst recommends waiting until SpaceX proves its AI investments are not just a money pit before investing.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The article expresses caution about SpaceX's investment thesis due to massive and widening AI segment losses ($3.73B in H1 2026) that are offsetting Starlink's profitability. The high 49x sales valuation combined with capital-intensive AI spending and rising interest rate concerns make the stock unattractive until the AI business proves viable.

title: Stock Market Today, Oct. 9: AT&T Slides on SpaceX Spectrum Deal Threat
author: Will Healy
description: SpaceX's acquisition of 800 MHz low-band spectrum triggered a sharp selloff in legacy wireless carriers on October 9, 2026. AT&T dropped 9.81%, Verizon fell 8.75%, and T-Mobile declined 13.27% as investors worried about increased competition and the erosion of the telecom oligopoly. However, analysts note AT&T's strong dividend yield (5%) and fiber infrastructure may provide some downside protection.
